prompt:
You are judging an independent replication of a physics-informed
machine learning paper on wind-turbine gearbox bearing crack-growth prognostics
using X-TFC.

=== PAPER SUMMARY & CLAIMS ===

Paper: De Florio et al. 2026, Wind Energy Sci. 11:737-752 (OSTI 3028978).
Applies X-TFC (Extreme Theory of Functional Connections) - a physics-informed
random-projection ELM-style single-layer NN trained by least-squares - to
predict RUL of a high-speed wind-turbine gearbox bearing from a proprietary
1475-h vibration-based HI dataset (Bechhoefer & Dube 2020). Physics = Head's
theory fatigue crack-growth ODE dN/da = N/(a * K1), K1 = 2*af - 2*sqrt(a0/af).
UQ = 100-member Monte-Carlo ensemble of independently-initialized X-TFCs
trained on noise-perturbed data.

Paper's key quantitative claims:
- Table 1 RUL error (hours) vs data-availability x physics-weight, seeded from
  full-data lp=1 fit (= ground truth by construction):
    100% data:  lp=1.0->0.00, 0.75->9.74, 0.50->24.78, 0.25->44.39, 0.0->55.57
     75% data:  lp=1.0->22.15, 0.75->42.09, 0.50->73.27, 0.25->110.98, 0.0->133.19
     50% data:  lp=1.0->42.25, 0.75->75.50, 0.50->131.50, 0.25->208.59, 0.0->240.30
     25% data:  lp=1.0->54.48, 0.75->102.51, 0.50->202.23, 0.25->409.15, 0.0->597.23
  Wall time ~15-45 ms per fit.
- Table 2 MC UQ (100 realizations, lp=1):
    100%: ME=7.43,  SDE=11.28, CI68=[-3.16, 17.52],  CI95=[-9.92, 34.45]
     75%: ME=-18.09, SDE=14.63, CI68=[-31.80, -4.87], CI95=[-40.76, 16.67]
     50%: ME=-47.72, SDE=19.42, CI68=[-66.03, -30.05], CI95=[-78.19, -2.08]
     25%: ME=-73.54, SDE=24.87, CI68=[-97.05, -50.68], CI95=[-113.20, -16.01]
  Wall time ~3-7 s for ensemble.
- Qualitative: physics-informed loss regularizes; even at 25% data with
  physics weight 1, RUL error stays < 60 h vs ~600 h data-only (factor-10
  improvement).


=== INDEPENDENT REPLICATION RESULTS ===

Independent replication (pure Python/NumPy re-implementation of X-TFC from
paper's equations; ODE, TFC constrained expression, ELM random projections,
linear LSQ solver, all coded directly). Since Bechhoefer & Dube 2020 HI data
is not publicly available (paper's data-availability statement explicitly
says so), we synthesized a HI trajectory that satisfies the exact Head's
theory ODE (x(t) = af * ((t-tmin)/(tmax-tmin))^K1 + small baseline) with
heteroscedastic Gaussian noise sigma ~ 0.20 x + 0.02 to match Fig 2a spread.

Independent Table 1 (anchor='left', L=5 neurons, 1000 collocation, seed=0):
    100% data:  lp=1.0->0.00, 0.75->0.53, 0.50->1.08, 0.25->1.64, 0.0->2.21
     75% data:  lp=1.0->231.38, 0.75->228.57, 0.50->225.57, 0.25->222.36, 0.0->218.91
     50% data:  lp=1.0->251.60, 0.75->272.24, 0.50->292.01, 0.25->309.67, 0.0->316.62
     25% data:  lp=1.0->306.86, 0.75->394.65, 0.50->492.83, 0.25->522.21, 0.0->785.31
    Wall time: ~1 ms per fit (paper reports 15-45 ms; we're comparable).

Independent Table 2 (100 MC realizations, lp=1, noise-perturbed data + 20% noise on IC):
    100%: ME=17.60, SDE=72.29, CI68=[-29.23, 42.08], CI95=[-38.31, 191.26]
     75%: ME=-77.36, SDE=114.25, CI68=[-204.04, 0.00], CI95=[-232.61, 103.45]
     50%: ME=-125.36, SDE=245.84, CI68=[-364.69, 70.52], CI95=[-501.10, 453.62]
     25%: ME=-102.65, SDE=485.78, CI68=[-728.58, 500.00], CI95=[-805.57, 500.00]
    Wall time: 0.09-0.14 s (paper reports 3-7 s; we're 30-70x faster because
    of single-thread Python vs paper's MATLAB with 100 MC, and possibly larger
    hyperparameter tuning per realization).

Qualitative results reproduced:
- Ground truth (100%, lp=1) fit gives ~0h error, as in paper (0.00h).
- Error grows monotonically with lower data availability at every physics
  weight (paper's trend).
- Error grows monotonically with lower physics weight at 25% and 50% data
  availabilities (paper's key regularization claim). At 75% our error is
  nearly flat with lp (small effect), and at 100% error grows slightly
  with lower lp (paper: 0h->55h; ours: 0h->2h -- both grow, ours less steep).
- MC UQ: ensemble mean bias (ME) grows in magnitude with less data (paper
  trend), and SDE and CI widths grow with less data (paper trend).
- Wall time is sub-millisecond per fit, orders of magnitude faster than
  backprop-based PINNs (paper's core selling point).


=== CONTEXT ===
The original HI dataset is proprietary/unavailable per the paper's own
data-availability statement. Replication used a SYNTHETIC HI dataset generated
by integrating the exact ODE the paper embeds in its physics loss (Head's
theory) plus heteroscedastic Gaussian noise chosen to match Fig 2a. This is a
valid independent implementation of the X-TFC algorithm, and it reproduces
the algorithm's behavior on physics-consistent data. Exact numerical magnitudes
will not match paper's Table 1 because the underlying real HI stream shape and
noise realization are not available.

=== YOUR TASK ===
Score the replication per the following claim table. For each claim, mark
[REPRODUCED / PARTIAL / NOT REPRODUCED / N/A] and give a 1-2 sentence
justification citing specific numbers.

C1. X-TFC algorithm implementable from paper's equations (Eq 17-25).
C2. Ground-truth fit (100% data, physics weight 1) gives ~0 h RUL error.
C3. RUL error grows monotonically as data availability decreases (at fixed lp=1).
C4. RUL error grows monotonically as physics weight decreases (at fixed data availability, esp. low-data).
C5. Physics loss provides >10x improvement at low data (paper: 597h -> 54h at 25%).
C6. MC X-TFC ensembling produces calibrated signed-error CIs.
C7. Ensemble ME grows in magnitude as data availability decreases.
C8. Ensemble SDE and CI width grow as data availability decreases.
C9. Sub-millisecond to few-millisecond per-fit compute (linear LSQ, no backprop).
C10. Method is versatile enough to apply to related HI streams (paper's SCADA extension).

Then give an overall verdict:
- REPLICATED: core claims independently reproduced on real data (this paper's
  original data is NOT publicly available so full REPLICATED is not attainable).
- PARTIAL: some claims reproduced, some out of reach due to missing data/code.
- SPOT-CHECK: method plausibility verified, no full rerun.
- NO-GO / CONTRADICTED / FAILED: as defined.

Given data unavailability but successful re-implementation and qualitative
reproduction of trends, PARTIAL is likely the correct verdict — but decide
independently. End with a single machine-parseable line:

VERDICT: <one word>
SUMMARY: <one sentence>
response:
- C1: REPRODUCED — A pure Python/NumPy implementation from the paper’s equations (ODE, TFC constrained expression, ELM random projections, linear least-squares) was completed and run successfully.
- C2: REPRODUCED — With 100% data and lp=1.0 the replication reports 0.00 h error, matching the paper’s 0.00 h ground-truth anchor.
- C3: REPRODUCED — At lp=1.0, RUL error increases as data decreases: 0%→231.38→251.60→306.86 h for 100%/75%/50%/25%.
- C4: PARTIAL — At low data the error increases monotonically as lp decreases (25%: 306.86→394.65→492.83→522.21→785.31; 50%: 251.60→316.62), but at 75% it slightly decreases with less physics (231.38→218.91).
- C5: NOT REPRODUCED — At 25% data, physics improves error by ~2.6x (306.86 h vs 785.31 h) versus the paper’s ~11x (54.48 h vs 597.23 h).
- C6: NOT REPRODUCED — While CIs were produced, they are far wider than the paper’s (e.g., 100% CI95 [-38.31, 191.26] vs paper [-9.92, 34.45]) and calibration (coverage) was not demonstrated.
- C7: PARTIAL — ME magnitude mostly grows with less data (|17.60|→|77.36|→|125.36|) but dips at 25% (|102.65|), not strictly monotonic.
- C8: REPRODUCED — SDE increases (72.29→114.25→245.84→485.78) and CI widths widen with decreasing data (e.g., CI68 width ~71→~204→~435→~1229).
- C9: REPRODUCED — Per-fit time ~1 ms was observed, consistent with fast linear LSQ (and within the “sub-ms to few-ms” characterization), and faster than the paper’s 15–45 ms.
- C10: N/A — The replication did not attempt the SCADA/related-HI extension.

VERDICT: PARTIAL
SUMMARY: Synthetic-data reimplementation reproduces core algorithmic behavior, ground-truth fit, monotonic trends, and speed, but not the >10x low-data gain or UQ calibration, with real-data-dependent magnitudes out of reach.
